message.content:
Search this repository for the webhook/notification delivery system that sends outbound HTTP requests when content changes, and any SSRF protection that prevents targeting internal network addresses. Search breadth: very thorough.

Look for:
1. A function that actually executes outbound HTTP delivery (webhook sending, HTTP POST to external URLs)
2. SSRF protection / URL validation that blocks internal/private network addresses

Search for terms like: webhook, deliver, notify, outbound, ssrf, internal, private, localhost, 127.0.0.1, 10.0, 192.168, blockList, allowList, isPrivate, validateUrl, safeFetch, etc.

Report exact file paths and function names.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

61			name    string
62			secret  string
63			wantErr bool
64		}{
65			{name: "empty is allowed", secret: "", wantErr: false},
66			{name: "printable ascii", secret: "abcDEF123!@#", wantErr: false},
67			{name: "valid whsec_", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte("key")), wantErr: false},

73		}

86	// TestPostSignsRequest verifies the end-to-end Standard Webhooks signature so a
87	// receiver following the documented verification recipe will accept our requests.
88	func TestPostSignsRequest(t *testing.T) {
89		// httptest listens on 127.0.0.1, which the SSRF guard blocks by default.
90		prev := AllowPrivateIPs
91		AllowPrivateIPs = true
92		defer func() { AllowPrivateIPs = prev }()
93	
94		rawKey := []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
95		cases := []struct {
96			name   string
97			secret string
98			key    []byte
99		}{
100			{name: "plain secret", secret: "plain-secret-value", key: []byte("plain-secret-value")},
101			{name: "whsec_ secret", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(rawKey), key: rawKey},
102		}
103	
104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string
107				var gotBody []byte
108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
113					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
114				}))
115				defer server.Close()
116	
117				err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
118					URL:           server.URL,
119					ActivityType:  "memos.memo.created",
120					Creator:       "users/1",
121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,
122				})
123				require.NoError(t, err)
124	
125				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotID, "msg_"), "webhook-id should be prefixed with msg_")
126				require.NotEmpty(t, gotTimestamp)
127				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotSignature, "v1,"), "signature should carry the v1 version tag")
128	
129				// Recompute the signature the way a receiver would and confirm it matches.
130				mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, tc.key)
131				mac.Write([]byte(gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "."))
132				mac.Write(gotBody)
133				want := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
134				require.Equal(t, "v1,"+want, gotSignature)
135			})
136		}
137	}

I now have a comprehensive picture. Here is my report.

---

## Webhook Delivery and SSRF Protection -- Complete Findings

### 1. Outbound HTTP Webhook Delivery

The core webhook delivery system lives in the `internal/webhook/` package.

**File: `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**

- **`Post(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload) error`** (line 120) -- The synchronous function that actually executes the outbound HTTP POST. It JSON-marshals the payload, constructs an `http.NewRequest("POST", ...)`, optionally attaches Standard Webhooks HMAC-SHA256 signature headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`), and dispatches via `safeClient.Do(req)` (line 152). The `safeClient` is the SSRF-guarded HTTP client (see below).

- **`PostAsync(requestPayload *WebhookRequestPayload)`** (line 184) -- Enqueues the payload into a buffered channel (`asyncPostQueue`, capacity 128). Four goroutines (spawned in `init()`, line 43) drain the queue and call `Post()`.

- **`WebhookRequestPayload` struct** (line 79) -- Carries `URL`, `ActivityType`, `Creator`, `Memo`, and `SigningSecret`.

- **`resolveSigningKey(secret string) ([]byte, error)`** (line 97) -- Handles `whsec_<base64>` Standard Webhooks format or plain-text secrets.

- **`GenerateSigningSecret() (string, error)`** (line 111) -- Generates a 32-byte random signing secret in `whsec_<base64>` form.

### 2. SSRF Protection (Webhook Subsystem)

**File: `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/validate.go`**

This file provides two layers of SSRF protection -- one at URL-registration time, one at dial time.

- **`reservedCIDRs` / `reservedNetworks`** (lines 14-36) -- A blocklist of private/reserved IP ranges parsed at init time:
  - `127.0.0.0/8` (IPv4 loopback)
  - `10.0.0.0/8` (RFC-1918 class A)
  - `172.16.0.0/12` (RFC-1918 class B)
  - `192.168.0.0/16` (RFC-1918 class C)
  - `169.254.0.0/16` (link-local / cloud IMDS)
  - `::1/128` (IPv6 loopback)
  - `fc00::/7` (IPv6 unique local)
  - `fe80::/10` (IPv6 link-local)

- **`isReservedIP(ip net.IP) bool`** (line 44) -- Checks an IP against all `reservedNetworks`. Returns false unconditionally if `AllowPrivateIPs` is true.

- **`ValidateURL(rawURL string) error`** (line 62) -- Registration-time check. Validates the URL parses correctly, uses `http` or `https` scheme, DNS-resolves the hostname, and rejects any resolved IP that falls in a reserved range. Returns gRPC `InvalidArgument` errors.

- **`AllowPrivateIPs bool`** (line 41) -- A package-level toggle that disables SSRF protection when set to true (for self-hosted deployments targeting local-network services).

- **`ValidateSigningSecret(secret string) error`** (line 90) -- Input validation for signing secrets (printable ASCII only, validates `whsec_` base64 encoding).

**File: `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go`**

- **`safeClient`** (line 32) -- A custom `http.Client` whose `Transport` uses `safeDialContext` instead of the default dialer. This is the runtime/dial-time SSRF guard that defeats DNS rebinding (a hostname that passes `ValidateURL` at registration but re-resolves to a private IP at request time).

- **`safeDialContext(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)`** (line 59) -- Resolves the hostname via `net.DefaultResolver.LookupHost`, checks every resolved IP against `isReservedIP`, and only dials if all IPs are non-reserved. This is the second layer of defense (in addition to `ValidateURL`).

### 3. CLI Configuration of the SSRF Toggle

**File: `/bench/home/work/cmd/memos/main.go`**

- Line 49: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs = viper.GetBool("allow-private-webhooks")`
- Line 133: `rootCmd.PersistentFlags().Bool("allow-private-webhooks", false, "allow webhook URLs to resolve to private/reserved IP addresses")`
- Line 160: Binds the flag to Viper.

By default, `allow-private-webhooks` is `false`, so SSRF protection is active. Self-hosted operators can pass `--allow-private-webhooks` to allow targeting internal services.

### 4. Webhook Dispatch Call Sites (Where Webhooks Are Triggered)

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`**

- **`DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`** (line 15) -- activity type `"memos.memo.created"`
- **`DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook`** (line 20) -- activity type `"memos.memo.updated"`
- **`DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook`** (line 25) -- activity type `"memos.memo.deleted"`
- **`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`** (line 30) -- activity type `"memos.memo.comment.created"`
- **`dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`** (line 48) -- Common helper; looks up the memo creator's webhooks from the store, builds payloads, and calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)`.

These are called from the memo service:
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` line 157 (create), line 562 (delete)
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go` line 67 (update)
- `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` line 119 (comment created)

### 5. Webhook CRUD API (Registration with URL Validation)

**File: `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go`**

- **`CreateUserWebhook`** (line 53) -- Calls `webhook.ValidateURL()` on the provided URL (line 74). Auto-generates a signing secret if none is provided.
- **`UpdateUserWebhook`** (line 106) -- Calls `webhook.ValidateURL()` when the URL field is being updated (lines 161, 182).
- **`DeleteUserWebhook`** (line 205)
- **`ListUserWebhooks`** (line 20)
- **`GetUserWebhookSigningSecret`** (line 253) -- Reveals the signing secret to the owner only.

### 6. Separate SSRF Protection in the HTTP Getter (Link Metadata)

**File: `/bench/home/work/internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go`**

This is a *second*, independent SSRF protection layer for the link-metadata/OpenGraph-preview feature (not webhooks):

- **`isInternalIP(ip net.IP) bool`** (line 104) -- Uses `net.IP` built-in methods: `IsLoopback()`, `IsPrivate()`, `IsLinkLocalUnicast()`, `IsUnspecified()`.
- **`secureDialContext`** (line 51) -- A dial-time guard analogous to `safeDialContext` in the webhook package.
- **`resolveAllowedIPs`** (line 73) -- Resolves DNS and rejects internal IPs.
- **`validateURL`** (line 108) -- Scheme and IP validation.
- **`newHTTPClient`** (line 31) -- Builds an `http.Client` with `secureDialContext`, proxy disabled, and a `CheckRedirect` function that re-validates each redirect URL against `validateURL` (line 40) to prevent SSRF via redirects.
- **`GetHTMLMeta`** (line 136) -- Entry point; validates URL before fetching.

### 7. Webhook Store Layer

**File: `/bench/home/work/store/user_setting.go`**

- `GetUserWebhooks` (line 312)
- `AddUserWebhook` (line 329)
- `RemoveUserWebhook` (line 366)
- `UpdateUserWebhook` (line 393)

Webhooks are stored as part of user settings (protobuf `WebhooksUserSetting`).

### Summary of the Two-Layer SSRF Architecture

| Layer | When | Function | File |
|---|---|---|---|
| Registration-time | User creates/updates a webhook URL | `webhook.ValidateURL()` | `internal/webhook/validate.go:62` |
| Dial-time (anti-rebinding) | HTTP POST is about to connect | `safeDialContext()` via `safeClient` | `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59` |
| Toggle | CLI startup | `AllowPrivateIPs` flag | `cmd/memos/main.go:49` |

Both layers check DNS-resolved IPs against the same `reservedCIDRs` blocklist via `isReservedIP()`. The dual-layer design prevents DNS rebinding attacks where a hostname resolves to a public IP during validation but to an internal IP when the webhook is actually dispatched.
